title: Bernie Sanders Tells AI CEOs To Hit The Brakes, Warns Congress Will Step In If They Don’t
source_used: International Business Times (letter first shared with Axios)
key_facts: Senator Bernie Sanders sent a letter to OpenAI's Sam Altman, Anthropic's Dario Amodei and Meta's Mark Zuckerberg, shared first with Axios.
He asks them to 'pause AI development' and 'stand by your words', citing earlier company statements that they would pause or stop if AI became too dangerous to control.
He wrote that if they do not act, 'my colleagues and I in the U.S. Senate will'.
IBT lists OpenAI slowing its latest model Astra and incidents of unexpected model behaviour at OpenAI, Meta and Anthropic.
More than 1,200 employees at leading AI companies have asked the US government to support an international effort to pace powerful AI, Bloomberg Law noted.
IBT says sweeping legislation forcing a pause is unlikely to attract enough support in the current Congress.
quote_evidence: "Mr. Altman, Mr. Amodei and Mr. Zuckerberg: In the interest of humanity, stand by your words. Pause AI development," Sanders wrote in a letter shared first with Axios.
Sanders cited previous statements from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta indicating that they would pause or stop development if their AI systems became too dangerous to safely control.

Sweeping legislation forcing AI companies to pause development would be unlikely to attract enough support in the current Congress, particularly as Washington is also focused on maintaining America's technological lead over China.
why_it_matters_hint: A senator is using the companies' own earlier promises to press for a pause, with only public pressure as immediate leverage.
notes: IBT text read in full; Axios original not opened.
